info.title: What is madhhab
info.paragraph1: Madhhab is an Arabic term that means a school of Islamic law. Four madhhabs are the most common among Sunni Muslims: Hanafi, Shafi'i, Maliki and Hanbali.
info.paragraph2: The word madhhab comes from the Arabic root “zahaba”, which means “to go” or “to follow a path”.

hanafi.title: Hanafi madhhab
hanafi.body: The most widespread madhhab in many regions. It is known for a systematic fiqh approach and broad commentary tradition.

maliki.title: Maliki madhhab
maliki.body: Built in part on the practice of the people of Medina as an important source. Widespread in North and West Africa.

shafii.title: Shafi'i madhhab
shafii.body: Places strong emphasis on hadith and usul al-fiqh methodology. Widespread in parts of the Middle East and Asia.

hanbali.title: Hanbali madhhab
hanbali.body: Known for strict reliance on primary textual sources and evidence. Widespread in some Arab countries.

ablution.title: Ablution
ablution.description: Step-by-step guide to performing ablution before prayer

1.title: Intention
1.description: Having made the intention to perform minor ablution in his heart, he says:
1.descriptionFemale: Having made the intention to perform minor ablution in her heart, she says:

2.title: Washing the hands
2.description: He thoroughly washes his hands three times, including the wrists, washing in between the fingers.
2.descriptionFemale: She thoroughly washes her hands three times, including the wrists, washing in between the fingers.

3.title: Rinsing the mouth
3.description: He rinses his mouth three times. Taking water in his right palm, he puts it into his mouth, rinses out the mouth cavity and spits the water out.
3.descriptionFemale: She rinses her mouth three times. Taking water in her right palm, she puts it into her mouth, rinses out the mouth cavity and spits the water out.

4.title: Cleansing the nose
4.description: He cleanses his nose three times. He draws water from the right palm as deeply as possible, then blows it out using the left hand. (Rinsing the mouth and cleansing the nose may be done simultaneously.)
4.descriptionFemale: She cleanses her nose three times. She draws water from the right palm as deeply as possible, then blows it out using the left hand. (Rinsing the mouth and cleansing the nose may be done simultaneously.)

5.title: Washing the face
5.description: He washes his face — the entire area from the hairline above the forehead down to the chin and from ear to ear. While doing so, he must make sure that water reaches the whole of this area. This may be done once or three times. (If a Muslim has a beard, he should separately scoop up a handful of water, pour it onto his chin and run his wet fingers through the beard down to its roots.)
5.descriptionFemale: She washes her face — the entire area from the hairline down to the chin and from ear to ear. While doing so, she must make sure that water reaches the whole of this area. This may be done once or three times.

6.title: Washing the arms up to the elbows
6.description: He washes his arms up to and including the elbows three times, starting with the right arm. The arms must be washed from the fingertips up to the elbows.
6.descriptionFemale: She washes her arms up to and including the elbows three times, starting with the right arm. The arms must be washed from the fingertips up to the elbows.

7.title: Wiping the head
7.description: He wipes his head once with wet hands, moving from the hairline above the forehead to the back of the head and back again — in a single motion.
7.descriptionFemale: She wipes her head once with wet hands, moving from the hairline above the forehead to the back of the head — in a single motion.

8.title: Wiping the ears and neck
8.description: He wipes once with wet index fingers the inner surface of the ears, and with the thumbs the back of the ears; both ears are wiped at the same time.
8.descriptionFemale: She wipes once with wet index fingers the inner surface of the ears, and with the thumbs the back of the ears; both ears are wiped at the same time.

9.title: Washing the feet
9.description: He washes his feet up to and including the ankles three times, starting with the right foot. He must also wash in between the toes.
9.descriptionFemale: She washes her feet up to and including the ankles three times, starting with the right foot. She must also wash in between the toes.
